01 / Decision guide AI-native programming languages: a practical comparison AI-native describes a design goal, not a safety certification. Compare what each language helps an agent do, which mistakes its tools can reject and what evidence you can inspect after a run. The right choice depends on your application and the guarantees it needs. Read the guide ↗

02 / Decision guide Programming languages for AI agents: choosing the host and tools Choose an agent’s host language by the tools it must call, the permissions those tools need and the failures it must recover from. The host coordinates the agent; the repository it edits can use another language. Test the interfaces between them before deciding whether any language change is needed. Read the guide ↗

03 / Decision guide AI code verification tools: what each check can establish Use independent checks tied to clear requirements to verify AI-generated code. A type checker rejects some invalid programs, a test checks selected behavior, and a proof establishes a stated property within its assumptions. An execution record helps show what ran. Build your verification process around the facts you need each tool to establish. Read the guide ↗

04 / Practical walkthrough Verify agent workflows: contracts, checks and reproducible evidence Check an agent’s completion report against the work it produced. Define the requirement first, inspect the output with an independent checker and keep the commands, results and environment details needed to repeat the check. This guide shows how to connect those steps using a small runnable example. Read the guide ↗
